items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
川魚のフナを、砂を落として洗った昆布でしっかりと巻き、大根やこんにゃく、れんこん、ごぼうなど季節の野菜とともに煮込む。姿のまま骨まで食べられるほどやわらかく仕上げるという。生臭さがなく独特の風味があるとされ、郷土食として愛されているそうだ。味の決め手は味噌からとるすめ汁だとされ、白石や佐賀平野のクリークでよく獲れるフナが使われるという。

## どう作るのか
味噌を袋に入れて自然にこし、すめ汁をとる。十分に砂を落とし洗った昆布でフナをきっちりと巻き、かんぴょうで結ぶ。大きめに切った大根やこんにゃくなどを鍋に入れひと煮立ちさせたら、フナを並べてすめ汁や水あめ、砂糖、醤油を加え、強火で長く煮込む。フナが常に水に浸っているよう注意するのだという。焦げないよう鍋底に藁を敷くこともあるそうだ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
冬の閑漁期に貴重なタンパク源として重宝されたフナを使った料理と伝わる。かつて恵比寿様に供える魚を、形の似たフナで間に合わせようとしたことが始まりとの説もあるという。ハレの日に大鍋でつくり、近隣にも配る習わしがあると語られている。鹿島市では二十日正月にこの料理を恵比寿様に供える風習も残っているそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
River-caught crucian carp is wound tightly in cleaned kelp and simmered with seasonal vegetables like daikon, konjac, lotus root, and burdock, cooked down until the whole fish, bones included, turns tender enough to eat. It's said to carry a distinctive flavor without any fishy smell, which is part of why it's so cherished as a local dish. The seasoning liquid strained from miso is said to be what makes or breaks the flavor.

## How it's made
Miso is hung in a cloth bag and left to strain naturally into a seasoning liquid. The fish is wound tightly in well-cleaned kelp and tied with a strip of dried gourd. Chunky-cut daikon, konjac, and other vegetables are brought to a boil in a pot, the wrapped fish is laid on top, and the strained miso liquid, starch syrup, sugar, and soy sauce are added before a long simmer over high heat, kept fully submerged the whole time. Straw is sometimes laid on the pot's bottom to keep things from scorching.

## Why it took this shape
The fish is said to have been valued as a source of protein during the quiet winter fishing season. One account holds the dish began when people substituted this similarly shaped fish for one usually offered to a local guardian deity. It's reportedly cooked in a big pot for celebratory occasions and shared around the neighborhood, and in one city the custom of offering it to that deity on a set winter date is said to continue today.

sources.title: ふなんこぐい 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
イカと大根や人参などの野菜を、白ごまと白味噌をベースにした衣であえたもの。地域や季節によっては、イワシやサバ、アジ、フナなど別の魚介を使うこともあるという。青魚を使う時は手開きにして軽く塩を振り、酢洗いしてから使うとされる。日常のおかずとして年間を通して食べられ、全国では「おろしなます」「かきあえ」などとも呼ばれる料理と似ているそうだ。

## どう作るのか
白ごまをよく炒ってすり、白味噌、砂糖、酢を順に加えてさらにすり込む。湯通ししたイカと、塩もみした大根や人参を短冊に切って和える。柚子胡椒や生姜を加えるアレンジもあるという。霜が降りる季節の大根は甘みが増すとされ、噛むほどに味わいが口に広がるという。ごまを丁寧にすることが仕上がりを左右し、使う魚介は家庭や地域によって異なるそうだ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
日常のおかずとして食べられる一方、お祭りや田植えなど人が集まる場でも欠かせない料理として伝わる。普段は質素な分、祭りの日にはいろいろな料理でもてなそうという思いも込められているという。秋祭りの頃は脂がのったサバを使うことがよくあり、堀やクリークの多い地域ではフナを使うこともあるそうだ。普段の粗食の反動で、ハレの日にはいろいろな料理を並べてもてなす習わしが根付いているという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Squid is tossed with vegetables like daikon and carrot in a dressing built on toasted sesame and white miso; depending on the area and season, other seafood such as sardine, mackerel, horse mackerel, or crucian carp is said to be used instead, hand-filleted, lightly salted, and rinsed in vinegar first when an oily fish is chosen. It's eaten as an everyday side dish throughout the year.

## How it's made
White sesame is roasted and ground well, then white miso, sugar, and vinegar are worked in one at a time. Blanched squid and salted, julienned daikon and carrot are cut into strips and tossed in the dressing, sometimes with yuzu pepper or ginger added. Daikon touched by early frost is said to turn especially sweet, its flavor spreading more the longer it's chewed. How well the sesame is ground is said to shape the final result.

## Why it took this shape
While it's an everyday side dish, it's also said to be indispensable at gatherings such as festivals or rice-planting days. Meals are often simple day to day, so the extra variety on festival days is said to carry a note of hospitality for guests. Around the time of the autumn festival, mackerel at its fattiest is often the fish of choice.

sources.title: いかのかけ和え 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
ミズイモの皮をむき、二杯酢や三杯酢に漬けた酢の物。シャキシャキとした食感を残すのが定番とされ、地域や家庭によって酸味や甘みが異なるという。干したずいきを使う場合は、もみながら水で戻してから調理するそうだ。冷蔵庫で1週間ほど保存できる常備菜だとされる。地元では夏の定番の味として長く親しまれてきたという。

## どう作るのか
ミズイモを切って水にさらしあくを抜く。酢や砂糖、輪切りの唐辛子を合わせた煮汁でさっと煮て、ショウガの千切りを天盛りする。煮すぎると食感が損なわれるため注意するという。干しずいきを使う場合は水で戻してから酢を加えてゆでる。よく冷やして食べると美味しいとされる。調味の加減は家庭によって少しずつ違うとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
暑さの厳しい佐賀の夏に重宝されてきた料理と伝わる。冷蔵庫でしばらく保存できることから常備菜としても親しまれ、お盆のお供えやお客をもてなす副菜としても出されてきたという。酸味や甘みの加減はそれぞれの家庭の味として受け継がれているそうだ。県内でも地域ごとに呼び名が異なることがあるという。冷蔵庫のない時代からの保存の知恵が今に伝わっているとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Mizuimo, a water taro, is peeled and steeped in a sweetened vinegar dressing; keeping its crisp, crunchy texture is considered standard, and the balance of sweet and tart is said to vary by household and region. When dried taro stem is used instead, it's rubbed and rehydrated in water first. It's said to keep for about a week in the refrigerator as a standing side dish. It's said to have long been cherished locally as a signature taste of summer.

## How it's made
The taro is cut and soaked in water to draw out bitterness, then briefly simmered in a mix of vinegar, sugar, and sliced chili before being topped with julienned ginger. Overcooking is said to spoil the crunch, so it's watched closely. Dried taro stem, when used, is rehydrated in water before vinegar is added and it's boiled, and the dish is said to taste best served well chilled. The exact seasoning is said to differ slightly from one household to the next.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to have long been valued during Saga's hot summers. Because it keeps for a while refrigerated, it's also become a household staple, served as an offering during the Bon festival or as a side when entertaining guests. The particular balance of tart and sweet is said to be passed down as each family's own recipe. The dish is also said to go by slightly different names depending on the area within the prefecture. It's described as a piece of preservation know-how passed down from a time before refrigerators.

sources.title: にいもじ 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
鶏肉と季節の野菜を、水をたっぷり使って仕上げる汁もの。慶事と弔事で具材の切り方が変わり、祝いごとでは四角、弔事では三角に切ることが多いという。地域によっては味付けに砂糖を使わない家庭もあるとされる。煮くずれしやすい食材は避けてつくられるという。福岡県にまたがって伝わる料理でもあるという。客をもてなす場面で長く親しまれてきた料理だという。

## どう作るのか
大根やこんにゃく、ごぼう、人参、里芋などを角切りや短冊切りにして下処理し、だしでやわらかく煮て塩や薄口醤油で味を調える。手まり麩やぎんなんを加え、片栗粉でとろみをつけることもあるという。とろみをつけずに仕上げる地域もあるそうだ。薄味でさっと仕上げるのがこつとされる。各家庭によって味付けが少しずつ異なるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
煮くずれしやすい食材を避け、水をたくさん入れて仕上げることから訛った名がついたと伝わる。冠婚葬祭で人を招く際に欠かせない料理で、かつては近隣の人が集まって共同で大量につくっていたという。慶事には玉麩、弔事にはこんにゃくを三角に切るなど、地域ごとの違いも語られているそうだ。かつては隣近所が集まり一度に大量につくっていたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Chicken and seasonal vegetables are cooked into a soup made with plenty of water; how the ingredients are cut is said to change with the occasion, often square for celebrations and triangular for funerals, and some households are said to leave sugar out of the seasoning altogether. Ingredients that fall apart easily when simmered are avoided by design. It's also said to be a dish shared across the border into neighboring Fukuoka prefecture. It's said to have long been cherished as a dish for entertaining guests.

## How it's made
Daikon, konjac, burdock, carrot, and taro are cut into cubes or strips and parboiled, then simmered in dashi until tender and seasoned with salt or light soy sauce. Wheat gluten balls and ginkgo nuts are sometimes added, with a light cornstarch thickening, though some areas are said to leave the broth unthickened instead, keeping the seasoning light and the finish quick. The exact seasoning is said to vary a little from one household to the next.

## Why it took this shape
Ingredients prone to falling apart are avoided, and the dish is finished with plenty of water, a style the name is said to reflect once slurred over time. It's considered essential when hosting guests for a life event, and it's said neighbors once gathered to make a large batch together. Local custom is also said to vary the cut of ingredients, such as wheat gluten flowers for celebrations and triangular konjac for funerals. It's said neighbors once gathered to make a large batch of it together.

sources.title: だぶ 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
番茶や粉茶で炊いたおかゆ。白がゆとは違い、茶の味が染み込んださっぱりとした味わいで、お茶の作用で粘り気が少なく、さらりと仕上がるとされる。季節によってはサツマイモを加えて「芋がゆ」にすることもあるという。夏は冷やして食べるのもよいとされる。有明海沿岸を中心に食習慣として根付いてきたと伝わる。嬉野では地元産の茶を使ってつくられているそうだ。

## どう作るのか
湯を沸かして番茶を加えて茶汁をつくり、そこに洗った米を加えて炊く。冷やごはんと袋に入れた茶葉を煮込む方法もあり、季節によってはサツマイモを加えてかさを増やすこともあるという。吹きこぼれないよう火加減に注意しながら炊くのがこつとされる。出がらしのお茶を無駄にしない知恵とも語られている。湯に冷やごはんを加えて煮込む方法も伝わっている。

## なぜこの形になったのか
米を大切にする倹約の心から生まれたと伝わる料理で、多くの使用人を抱えた商家では前夜の冷やごはんと出がらしのお茶を使い、朝食として振る舞われていたという。現在は県内の宿の朝食で味わえることがあるそうだ。嬉野など茶どころではその土地の茶を使ってつくられているという。経済成長とともに家庭でつくられることは減っていったそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This porridge is cooked in roasted or powdered green tea rather than water; unlike plain rice porridge, it carries the tea's flavor and finishes light and smooth, since the tea is said to keep it from turning sticky. Sweet potato is sometimes added depending on the season, turning it into a potato porridge, and it's also said to be good served chilled in summer. It's said to have taken root as a food custom mainly along the Ariake coast. In one hot-spring town it's said to be made with locally grown tea.

## How it's made
Water is boiled and roasted tea added to make a tea broth, into which washed rice is added and cooked. There's also a method using leftover rice with tea leaves in a bag simmered in, and sweet potato is sometimes added to bulk it out depending on the season. Watching the heat carefully so it doesn't boil over is said to be the key step. It's also described as a clever way to make use of tea leaves already brewed once. There's also a method of simmering leftover cold rice directly in hot water.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to have grown out of a spirit of thrift toward rice. In merchant households with many employees, it's said to have been served for breakfast using the previous night's cold rice and tea leaves already brewed once. It can still be found today served at breakfast in some inns around the prefecture, and in tea-growing towns it's said to be made with locally grown tea. It's said to have been made at home less often as the economy grew.

sources.title: お茶がい／茶がゆ 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
里芋やごぼうなど根菜がたっぷり入り、片栗粉でとろみをつけた汁もの。行事によって鶏肉やあずき、花麩など加える具材が変わるという。体を温める冬の一品として、日常的に食べられてきたと伝わる。とろみのある口当たりが特徴の家庭料理だとされる。「のっぺい汁」や「ぬっぺい汁」とも呼ばれることがあるという。冬の体を温める汁として日常的に親しまれてきたという。

## どう作るのか
里芋やさつまいも、ごぼう、れんこんをさいの目に切ってゆで、鶏肉やかまぼこなども同様に切る。だしで煮て塩や醤油で味を調え、水溶き片栗粉でとろみをつける。彩りに豆麩やグリンピースを添えることもあるという。だしは昆布や鶏ガラ、干しシイタケなどでとるそうだ。彩りにグリンピースを散らすこともあるそうだ。昆布や鶏ガラなど、だしのとり方にも工夫があるそうだ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
祝いの日には鶏肉、結婚などのめでたい席ではあずき、供養の席では肉を使わず花麩を入れるなど、行事ごとに具材を変える習わしがあるという。仏事にはしいたけとごぼうを味出しとして使うことが多いと伝わる。揚げ豆腐のしめ汁を使って煮込むこともあるそうだ。野菜など具だくさんで、味付けは変わらず醤油や塩とされる。行事によって加える具材が丁寧に使い分けられているという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This soup is packed with root vegetables like taro and burdock and thickened with potato starch; the ingredients added are said to shift depending on the occasion, from chicken to red beans to wheat gluten flowers. It's said to have long been eaten as an everyday dish to warm the body in winter, its thickened texture the dish's signature trait. It's also sometimes called by a couple of slightly different local names. It's said to have been cherished as an everyday soup for warming the body in winter.

## How it's made
Taro, sweet potato, burdock, and lotus root are diced and parboiled, and chicken or fish cake is cut the same way. Everything simmers in dashi, seasoned with salt or soy sauce, and thickened with a potato-starch slurry, sometimes finished with wheat gluten cubes or green peas for color. The dashi is said to draw on kelp, chicken bones, or dried shiitake. Green peas are sometimes scattered on top for color. The dashi itself is said to be drawn with care from kelp or chicken bones.

## Why it took this shape
Custom holds that chicken goes in for celebrations, red beans for happy occasions like weddings, and flower-shaped wheat gluten without meat for memorial gatherings. For Buddhist observances, shiitake and burdock are said to be favored for the flavor they lend the broth. The cooking liquid left from simmering fried tofu is sometimes worked in too. The soup is always packed with vegetables, seasoned simply with soy sauce or salt. The ingredients added are said to be carefully chosen to suit each occasion.

sources.title: のっぺ汁 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
鶏肉や小豆、栗とともに、れんこんやごぼう、大根などの根菜を砂糖や醤油で煮含めた料理。別の呼び名でも呼ばれ、根菜の素朴な味わいと栄養のバランスの良さが魅力とされる。くんち前夜にたくさんつくり、数日かけて食べるという。伊万里の秋祭りに欠かせない一皿だとされる。「煮じゃあ」「煮じゃー」とも呼ばれているという。

## どう作るのか
鶏もも肉と根菜を同じくらいの大きさの乱切りにし、こんにゃくは下ゆでしてちぎる。小豆はゆでこぼしてから再びやわらかく煮る。だしに具材を入れて煮て、小豆とそのゆで汁、調味料を加えて味を調える。鶏肉の代わりに魚介やだんごを使うこともあるそうだ。じっくり味を含ませるのがこつとされる。地域によっては魚介を使うこともあるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
秋祭りの前夜にたくさんつくり、数日かけて温め直しながら食べる料理と伝わる。もとは煮しめの残り材料と、栗おこわに使う栗や小豆のゆで汁を無駄にしないために生まれたといわれている。祭りに招いた客にはきれいな形の材料を、家族の分は切りくずを使うこともあったそうだ。太鼓の音にちなんだ呼び名を持つ祭りとして知られているそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Chicken, red beans, and chestnuts are simmered together with root vegetables like lotus root, burdock, and daikon in sugar and soy sauce; also known by another local name, it's valued for the plain, honest taste of its vegetables and its well-rounded nutrition. It's said to be made in a big batch the night before a festival and eaten over several days, an essential dish for one city's autumn festival. It's also known by a couple of other local names tied to the sound of simmering.

## How it's made
Chicken thigh and root vegetables are cut into similarly sized rough chunks, and konjac is parboiled and torn by hand. Red beans are boiled once, drained, and simmered again until soft. The vegetables simmer in dashi, then the beans, their cooking liquid, and seasoning are added to finish. Seafood or dumplings are sometimes used in place of the chicken, and letting the flavor soak in slowly is said to be the key. Seafood is sometimes used in place of chicken depending on the area.

## Why it took this shape
It's said to be made in a large batch the night before an autumn festival and eaten over several days, reheated each time. One account holds it began as a way to use up leftovers from a simmered dish along with the chestnuts, red beans, and cooking liquid meant for a chestnut rice dish, so nothing went to waste. Neatly cut pieces were reportedly saved for guests, with odd scraps kept for the family. The festival it's tied to is known locally by a nickname referencing the sound of its drums.

sources.title: 煮ごみ 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
鶏肉と根菜をたっぷり使った煮物。れんこんやごぼう、こんにゃく、しいたけなどを炒めてから煮含める、佐賀の定番の郷土料理とされる。おくんちなどの祭りや正月の祝い事に欠かせない行事食として受け継がれてきたという。彩りにさやえんどうを添えることも多いそうだ。全国的には「筑前煮」の名でも知られているという。地元では欠かせない定番の郷土料理として親しまれている。

## どう作るのか
戻したしいたけ、下ゆでしたれんこんやごぼう、こんにゃくを用意し、鶏肉を炒めてから他の具材を加えてさっと炒める。しいたけの戻し汁と調味料を加え、あくを取りながら弱火で煮含め、筋を取ってゆでたさやえんどうを添える。針しょうがを添えることもあるという。下ゆでや油炒めなど、下ごしらえに手間をかけるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
すっぽんを煮て食べたのが始まりと伝わる料理で、今では鶏肉を使うのが一般的になっている。祭りや祝いの席に欠かせない郷土料理で、正月にはおせち料理のひとつとして食卓に並ぶという。福岡をはじめ九州の他地域でも同様の料理が親しまれているそうだ。博多をはじめ九州各地でも親しまれている料理だという。正月のおせちの一品としても食卓に並ぶそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Chicken and plenty of root vegetables come together in this simmered dish, a Saga staple said to be made by stir-frying lotus root, burdock, konjac, and shiitake before simmering them through. It's been carried on as festive fare for autumn shrine festivals and New Year's celebrations alike, often finished with snap peas for color. It's also widely known nationally under a different regional name. It's cherished locally as an indispensable local staple.

## How it's made
Rehydrated shiitake, parboiled lotus root and burdock, and konjac are prepared, then chicken is stir-fried and the other ingredients added briefly. The shiitake soaking liquid and seasoning go in, and everything simmers slowly over low heat, skimmed as needed, finished with snap peas that have had their strings removed and been parboiled. Fine shreds of ginger are sometimes added on top too. Parboiling and stir-frying the ingredients first is said to take real care in the prep work.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to trace back to a time when soft-shelled turtle was simmered instead, though chicken is standard today. It's considered an essential dish for festivals and celebrations, and it's said to take its place on the table as part of the New Year's osechi spread. Similar versions are said to be cherished across other parts of Kyushu as well. Similar dishes are said to be cherished across Kyushu, including in neighboring Fukuoka. It's also said to take its place on the table as part of the New Year's osechi spread.

sources.title: がめ煮 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
泥の中にすむ有明海特有の魚、ムツゴロウを素焼きにしてから甘辛く炊いたもの。鮮度のよいものは刺身や味噌汁にすることもあるという。産卵期の5月から7月にかけて旬を迎え、伝統漁法で釣り上げられるという。エラと皮膚の両方で呼吸できる珍しい魚だとされる。地元では単に「ムツ」と呼ばれることもあるという。求愛行動でジャンプする様子を写真に収めようと人が集まるという。

## どう作るのか
生きたムツゴロウを串に刺して炭火で素焼きにする。砂糖、醤油、酒を合わせた鍋に加え、煮汁がなくなるまでじっくり煮る。活きのよいものは塩水に漬けて泥を吐かせておくという。この蒲焼を巻いた寿司として食べられることもあるそうだ。じっくり煮詰めて味を含ませるのがこつとされる。泥を吐かせる下ごしらえが臭みを抑えるこつだとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
干満差の大きい有明海の干潟でしかとれない魚とされ、潮が引いた時に伝統漁法で釣り上げられると伝わる。素焼きにしてから甘辛く炊く食べ方が郷土料理として親しまれてきたという。オスがメスへの求愛でジャンプを繰り返す様子を見に、全国から人が集まるとも語られている。有明海と八代海の一部にしか生息しないとされる希少な魚だという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Mudskipper, a fish unique to the Ariake Sea's muddy flats, is plain-grilled and then simmered in a sweet-savory sauce; when especially fresh, it's said to be eaten as sashimi or in miso soup instead. It comes into season from May to July during its spawning period, caught with a traditional method, and it's an unusual fish that can breathe through both its gills and its skin. Locally the fish is sometimes simply called mutsu for short. People are said to gather just to photograph the males leaping in their courtship display.

## How it's made
The live fish is skewered and plain-grilled over charcoal, then added to a pot of sugar, soy sauce, and sake and simmered slowly until the liquid is gone. Especially lively fish are said to be soaked in salt water first to purge the mud, and the grilled fish is also said to be rolled into a sushi variant. Letting the sauce reduce slowly is said to be the key to working the flavor all the way through. Purging the mud out first is said to be the key step for keeping the flavor clean.

## Why it took this shape
The fish is said to live only on the tidal flats of the Ariake Sea, caught with a traditional method as the tide goes out. Grilling it plain before simmering it sweet and savory is said to have become the region's cherished way of preparing it. Visitors are said to travel from across the country just to watch the males leap repeatedly to court females during spawning season. The fish is said to live nowhere in Japan except the Ariake Sea and part of one other bay.

## 何でできているか
小麦粉を練った生地をゆで、黒砂糖をまぶした素朴なおやつ。生地にゆでたかぼちゃやほうれん草、よもぎを混ぜたり、あんこを包むこともあるという。風味豊かに仕上がるのは黒砂糖だとされる。地域によっては「平だご」とも呼ばれているそうだ。小麦粉と米粉の両方でつくられることがあるという。農家で常備されていた小麦粉を使う素朴な菓子だという。

## どう作るのか
小麦粉に熱湯を合わせて耳たぶほどの硬さにこね、生地をちぎりながら沸騰した湯に入れてゆでる。ゆで汁を捨てて黒砂糖をまぶす。おかゆをつぶして混ぜると時間が経ってもやわらかいままになるという。米粉でつくり砂糖醤油をつけることもあるそうだ。生地の形は家庭によってさまざまだという。祭りで振る舞われることもあったと伝わる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
米の裏作として麦を育てる二毛作が盛んな土地で、常備してあった小麦粉を使ったおやつとして親しまれてきたと伝わる。農作業の合間の一息や、ごはんが足りない時の補食として食べられていたという。武雄地区では田植え時の休憩でよく食べられていたとも伝わっている。農作業の合間の一息に欠かせないおやつだったという。武雄地区では田植え時の休憩でよく食べられていたとも伝わる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
A simple dumpling made by boiling kneaded wheat dough and dusting it with brown sugar; the dough is sometimes mixed with boiled pumpkin, spinach, or mugwort, or wrapped around sweet bean paste instead. Brown sugar is said to give the best, most fragrant result, and in some areas the dumpling goes by another flatter-sounding local name. It's said to be made from either wheat flour or rice flour depending on the household. It's a simple sweet made from the wheat flour farming households always kept on hand.

## How it's made
Wheat flour is kneaded with boiling water to an earlobe-soft dough, torn into pieces, and dropped into boiling water to cook. The cooking water is drained off and brown sugar dusted over. Mixing in mashed rice porridge is said to keep the dumplings soft even after time passes, and a rice-flour version dipped in sweetened soy sauce is also made, its shape varying from one household to the next. It's also said to have once been served at local festivals.

## Why it took this shape
In a region where wheat was grown as a second crop after rice, the snack is said to have taken hold using the flour households always had on hand, eaten as a break during farm work or to fill in when rice ran short. In one district it's said to have been a favorite bite during breaks from rice planting. It's said to have been an essential little break during a long day of farm work. In one district it's said to have been a favorite bite during breaks from rice planting.

## 何でできているか
里芋やほうれん草などの野菜を、味噌やごまで和えた白和え。豆腐の代わりに常備していたサトイモを使うようになったと伝わり、家庭によってかぼちゃを使うこともあるという。里芋のつぶし加減で食感を変える工夫もあるそうだ。女性の言葉で和え物を意味する名だとされる。現在では各家庭によって使う野菜や味付けが変わるという。

## どう作るのか
里芋をゆでてつぶしておく。ほうれん草はゆでて水気を絞る。だしで人参やごぼう、しいたけを煮て、つぶした里芋に砂糖やみりん、味噌、ごまを混ぜたものと合わせる。野菜の水気をしっかり切るのがこつだという。里芋は粉ふきいものように水分を飛ばすとよいとされる。かぼちゃを代用することもあるとされる。各家庭の味として受け継がれているとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
かつて集落を焼いた火災の際、焼け残った野草を和えて食べたという伝承にちなむ料理とされる。それ以来、先人の思いを忘れないよう毎年その日にこの料理をふるまう祭りが続いているという。佐賀のおふくろの味として、日常食にも取り入れられているそうだ。被災した先人の思いを忘れないための料理だと語り継がれている。先人の苦労を忘れないための料理として今に続くという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Vegetables such as taro and spinach are dressed like a tofu-based salad, but with mashed taro standing in for tofu, a substitution said to date back to using whatever vegetables a household had on hand; pumpkin sometimes replaces the taro too, and the taro is mashed more or less finely depending on the texture desired. The name is a local word for a dressed vegetable dish, said to come from women's speech. Today the vegetables and seasoning used are said to vary from one household to the next.

## How it's made
Taro is boiled and mashed. Spinach is boiled and squeezed dry. Carrot, burdock, and shiitake are simmered in dashi, then combined with the mashed taro mixed with sugar, mirin, miso, and sesame. Thoroughly draining the vegetables is said to be the key step, and drying the mashed taro the way one dries out boiled potatoes is said to help. Pumpkin is sometimes used as a substitute as well. It's said to be passed down as each family's own particular recipe.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is tied to a story about a fire that once burned through a local settlement, after which residents are said to have eaten wild greens dressed together to get by. A festival is still held each year on that date to keep the memory of that time alive, with this dish always served. It's also become a fixture of everyday home cooking across the prefecture. It's passed down as a dish meant to keep alive the memory of what earlier generations went through. It continues today as a dish meant to remember what those generations went through.

## 何でできているか
小麦粉でつくっただんごを、旬の野菜とともに煮込んだ汁もの。手でちぎってだんごをつくることから地元の言葉で名がついたと伝わる。麦づくりが盛んな土地で、米が足りない時の代用品として食べられてきたという。呼び名は地域によってさまざまだとされる。「だんご汁」や「ひらひぼ汁」など呼び名は地域で異なるという。地域や形状によって呼び名が変わる汁ものだとされる。

## どう作るのか
里芋や人参などの野菜を一口大に切り、だし汁で煮る。火が通ったら、耳たぶほどの硬さにこねた小麦粉のだんごを手でちぎりながら加え、味噌や醤油で味を調える。だんごに蒸したさつまいもを混ぜると冷めても硬くなりにくいという。鶏肉の代わりにクジラ肉を使う地域もあるそうだ。小豆を入れる地域もあると伝わる。旬の野菜を使うのが基本とされている。

## なぜこの形になったのか
田植えや稲刈りで朝から日暮れまで働く農家の、間食や夜食としても食べられていたという。昔は主食の一品であったが、現在では副食の位置づけで食べられることが多いと伝わる。熊本県や大分県、宮崎県など広い地域で親しまれている汁ものだとされる。熊本県や大分県、宮崎県でも親しまれている汁ものだという。農作業の合間の間食としても親しまれてきたそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Wheat-flour dumplings are simmered with vegetables in season; the local name is said to come from a dialect word for tearing, describing how the dumplings are pinched off by hand. In a region known for growing wheat, the dish is said to have served as a stand-in when rice ran short, and it goes by various names in different places. The dish goes by several different names depending on the area. The soup is said to go by different names depending on the dumpling's shape too.

## How it's made
Taro, carrot, and other vegetables are cut into bite-sized pieces and simmered in dashi. Once cooked through, dumplings kneaded from wheat flour to an earlobe-soft dough are torn in by hand, and the soup is seasoned with miso or soy sauce. Mixing steamed sweet potato into the dough is said to keep the dumplings soft even after cooling, and whale meat is sometimes used instead of chicken in some areas. Red beans are sometimes added in some areas as well. Using whatever vegetables are in season is considered the basic rule.

## Why it took this shape
It's also said to have been eaten as a snack or late meal by farming families working from dawn to dusk during planting and harvest. It was once treated as a main dish in its own right, though today it's more often eaten as a side. It's said to be enjoyed across a wide stretch of Kyushu beyond Saga as well. Similar soups are said to be cherished in neighboring Kumamoto, Oita, and Miyazaki too. It's also said to have been enjoyed as a snack between stretches of farm work.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
豆乳に葛やでんぷんを加えて固めた、通常の豆腐とは違うなめらかな食感が特徴の一品。ごま醤油をかけて副菜にするほか、黒蜜やきな粉でスイーツ風にも食べられるという。プリンのようなつやのある見た目だとされる。中国の国名にちなんだ名という説も伝わる。「呉」と呼ばれる大豆をすりつぶした状態が名の由来とされる。水に浸した大豆を石臼ですりつぶしてつくられるという。

## どう作るのか
豆乳を鍋で温め、でんぷんを水で溶いたものを加えて弱火で練り続ける。なめらかになったら火を止めてバットに流し込み、冷水で冷やす。ごま醤油や黒蜜をかけたり、衣をつけて揚げたり、味噌汁の具にすることもあるという。20分ほど練り続けるのがこつとされる。衣をつけて揚げる食べ方もあるという。冷水でしっかり冷やすとつやが増すとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
通常はにがりで固める豆腐を、葛やでんぷんで仕上げるようになった経緯には諸説あると伝わる。大豆を買い付けに訪れた土地で豆乳を葛で固める製法を教わり、地域に広まったという説が残っている。有田町を中心に昭和の初め頃から親しまれるようになったそうだ。昭和の初め頃に有田町へ広まったと伝わっている。中国から伝わった豆腐だからという説も残っている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Soy milk is set with kudzu or potato starch instead of the usual coagulant, giving it a smoother texture than regular tofu, glossy enough to be compared to pudding. It's served as a side with sesame-soy sauce, or dressed with black sugar syrup or soybean flour as a dessert. One account even ties the dish's name to a historical Chinese state. The name is said to come from a term for ground soybeans in that state before straining. It starts from soybeans soaked in water and ground on a stone mill.

## How it's made
Soy milk is warmed in a pot, and starch dissolved in water is stirred in and worked over low heat until smooth. It's then poured into a tray and chilled in cold water. It's typically topped with sesame-soy sauce or black sugar syrup, though it's sometimes battered and fried, or dropped into miso soup as well. Working the mixture for about twenty minutes is said to be the key step. It's also sometimes battered and deep-fried as another way to enjoy it. Chilling it firmly in cold water is said to bring out its glossy finish.

## Why it took this shape
Accounts differ on how tofu here came to be set with kudzu or starch instead of the usual coagulant. One story holds that someone who traveled elsewhere to buy soybeans learned a method of setting soy milk with kudzu there, and brought it back to spread through the area. It's said to have taken hold in one porcelain-making town from around the early twentieth century. It's said to have spread through the porcelain town from around the early twentieth century. One account even holds that the tofu originally came from China, giving it its name.

## 何でできているか
鬼おろしという竹製のおろし器で粗くおろした大根おろしと、焼いた餅や薄揚げを味噌汁に入れた汁もの。クジラ肉を入れることもあるという。窯焚きの夜食として重宝されてきたと伝わる。大根の粗さが独特の食感を生むとされる。地元では冬の定番の汁ものとして親しまれてきたという。陶山神社の年越し行事でも振る舞われているという。

## どう作るのか
だしをとって味噌を溶いた汁に、粗くおろした大根おろしを入れる。餅を香ばしく焼いて温まった汁に加える。薄揚げやクジラ肉を加えることもあるとされ、寒い夜に体を温める一杯として親しまれてきたという。焼いた餅の香ばしさが味の決め手になるそうだ。クジラ肉を入れる家庭もあるとされる。窯焚きの一晩を支える夜食として重宝されてきたそうだ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
焼き物の窯元で一晩中窯につく窯焚きの際、夜食として食べられていたと伝わる。体が温まり、腹持ちがよく食べやすいことから重宝されたのだという。現在は大晦日の行事で振る舞われているという。有田焼の里に伝わる冬ならではの一杯だとされる。有田焼の窯元に伝わる夜食の知恵として語られている。有田焼の窯元とともに歩んできた食文化だとされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Daikon coarsely grated with a bamboo grater called an oni-oroshi is added to a miso soup along with grilled mochi and fried tofu; whale meat is sometimes included as well. It's said to have been treasured as a late-night meal for potters tending a kiln. The daikon's coarse texture is said to give the soup its distinctive bite. It's said to have been cherished locally as a classic winter soup. It's also served at a local shrine's New Year's Eve lantern event.

## How it's made
Dashi is drawn and miso dissolved into it, then the coarsely grated daikon is stirred in. Mochi is grilled until fragrant and added to the warmed soup. Fried tofu or whale meat are sometimes folded in too, and it's said to have been cherished as a bowl to warm the body on a cold night, the toasted mochi said to be what ties the flavor together. Some households are said to add whale meat as well. It's said to have been valued as a late-night meal to get through a night of kiln-tending.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to have been eaten as a late-night meal by potters tending a kiln through the night. It's described as having been valued for warming the body, being filling, and being easy to eat under those conditions, and it's now served at a year-end local event. It's described as a winter bowl distinctive to a town known for its porcelain. It's described as a piece of late-night kitchen wisdom passed down among porcelain kiln workers. It grew up alongside the porcelain kilns themselves.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
有明海でとれるシタビラメを、佐賀では「くちぞこ」と呼ぶ。木の葉のような体形で、背びれや尾びれの区別がはっきりしないのが特徴とされる。少し甘辛く味をつけたたっぷりの調味液で煮付けにされることが多いという。ヒラメ類と近縁で両眼が体の左側にあるそうだ。有明海にはこの魚のほかにも固有の生物が多く生息するとされる。

## どう作るのか
うろこを取ったくちぞこを、醤油や酒、みりんを煮立てた煮汁で煮込み、野菜を加えて煮含める。少し甘辛く味をつけるのが定番とされ、一回り小さいものはから揚げにすると骨まで食べられるという。身離れがよいので調理しやすいとされる。一回り小さい種類はから揚げで骨まで食べられるという。離乳食や幼児向けの魚料理としても使われてきたそうだ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
広大な干潟を持つ有明海には、この魚をはじめ地域特有の魚介が多く生息すると伝わる。身離れがよいことから離乳食や幼児向けの魚料理としても使われてきたという。中でも黒い皮のものは特に旨味があるとされ、地元で好んで食べられているそうだ。旬は種類によって異なり、年間を通して流通しているとされる。地元では日常のおかずとして長く親しまれているという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Sole caught in the Ariake Sea is locally known as kuchizoko in Saga, its leaf-shaped body and indistinct dorsal and tail fins setting it apart from other flatfish. It's most often simmered in a generous, mildly sweet and savory seasoning liquid. It's a close relative of flounder, with both eyes set on the left side of its body. The Ariake Sea is said to be home to many other creatures found nowhere else too.

## How it's made
The scaled sole is simmered in a broth of boiled soy sauce, sake, and mirin, with vegetables added to simmer through. A mildly sweet, savory seasoning is considered the standard, and a smaller variety of the fish is said to be deep-fried whole, bones and all. The flesh is said to come off the bone easily, making it simple to prepare. A smaller variety of the fish is said to be deep-fried whole, bones and all. It's also said to have been used in cooking for infants and young children.

## Why it took this shape
The Ariake Sea, known for a vast tidal flat, is said to be home to this fish along with other creatures particular to the region. Because the flesh comes off the bone easily, it's also said to have been used in cooking for infants and young children. The dark-skinned variety in particular is said to carry an especially rich flavor, favored by locals. Different varieties come into season at different times, so it's available year-round. It's said to have long been cherished locally as an everyday side dish.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
もち米に栗と小豆を加えて蒸したおこわ。神前に供える際は円錐や三角のおにぎりの形にすることもあるという。新米を氏神様に捧げる秋祭りに欠かせない料理と伝わる。勝ち戦を願うかち栗を使うこともあるそうだ。「栗こわい」「こわい」とも呼ばれているという。秋祭りに訪れる客人への手土産としても長く定番だったという。

## どう作るのか
もち米は洗って一晩水につける。小豆は一度ゆでこぼしてから再びゆで、七、八分ほどの硬さに仕上げる。もち米と小豆を混ぜ、栗をのせて蒸し器で蒸し上げる。栗は干して臼で軽くついた保存食を使うこともあるという。蒸し加減で食感が変わるそうだ。小豆は一度ゆでこぼしてから使うのがこつとされる。神前に供える際は形にもこだわりがあるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
祭りの数日前から準備が始まり、客人への土産の定番としてもつくられてきたという。祭りだけでなく、お祝い事でも食された郷土料理で、地域や家庭によって作り方や味が異なるとされる。伊万里くんちなど、各地の秋祭りで欠かせない一品だとされる。有田では末広の形の木枠で抜いて提供することもあるという。地域によって具材や味つけに違いがあるそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Glutinous rice is steamed with chestnuts and red beans folded in; when offered at a shrine, it's sometimes shaped into cones or triangular rice balls. The dish is said to be indispensable at an autumn festival where new rice is offered to a local guardian deity. Chestnuts dried and lightly pounded, kept in hopes of a victorious outcome, are sometimes used. It's also known by a couple of other local names tied to the word for steamed rice. It was also traditionally given as a standard gift to festival guests.

## How it's made
The glutinous rice is washed and soaked overnight. Red beans are boiled once, drained, and boiled again until they reach a slightly firm texture. The rice and beans are mixed, topped with chestnuts, and steamed. Chestnuts dried and lightly pounded as a preserved food are sometimes used as well, and how long it's steamed is said to shape the final texture. Boiling the red beans once and draining them before the main cook is said to be the trick. Its shape is said to matter when it's offered at a shrine.

## Why it took this shape
Preparations reportedly begin days before the festival, and it's traditionally been made as a gift for visiting guests. Beyond festivals, it's also eaten at celebrations, and the recipe and flavor are said to vary from place to place. It's described as an essential dish at autumn festivals held across different towns in the prefecture. In one porcelain town it's said to be pressed into a fan-shaped mold before serving. The ingredients and seasoning are said to vary a little from place to place.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
大根と干し柿を千切りにし、酢やゆずのしぼり汁、砂糖、薄口醤油、塩で和えたなます。生の柿を使ったり、大根の代わりにかぶを使うこともあるという。柿づくりの盛んな山あいの土地で親しまれてきたとされる。もっちりとした独特の食感が魅力だという。樹齢の長い柿の木からとれる希少な品種もあるという。渋抜きの手間をかけた希少な柿も知られているという。

## どう作るのか
大根と干し柿を千切りにする。酢、ゆずのしぼり汁、砂糖、薄口醤油、塩を合わせ、千切りにした大根と干し柿を和える。ゆずの皮の千切りを加えることもあるという。冷凍保存もできることから近年は通年出回っているそうだ。柿の甘みと酸味のバランスが決め手とされる。ゆずの皮の千切りを添えると香りが引き立つとされる。冷凍保存によって通年味わえるようになったそうだ。

## なぜこの形になったのか
寒暖差の大きい山あいの土地が干し柿づくりに適しているとされ、軒先に吊るされた干し柿が秋の風物詩になっていると伝わる。干し柿の産地では、正月のなますにこの干し柿を使うのが欠かせない習わしだという。約300年前から続く風景だとも語られている。脊振山系や天山山系のふもとでよく見られる光景だという。軒先に吊るされた干し柿の景色が秋を告げるという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Daikon and dried persimmon are julienned and dressed in vinegar, yuzu citrus juice, sugar, light soy sauce, and salt; fresh persimmon is sometimes used instead of dried, and turnip can stand in for the daikon. It's said to be a dish cherished in mountain terrain known for growing persimmons, prized for its distinctively soft, chewy texture. Some rare persimmon varieties are said to come from especially old trees in the area. A rare, painstakingly de-astringed persimmon variety is also known locally.

## How it's made
Daikon and dried persimmon are cut into thin strips. Vinegar, yuzu juice, sugar, light soy sauce, and salt are combined and tossed with the julienned daikon and persimmon, sometimes with a bit of julienned yuzu peel added. Because it can also be frozen for storage, it's said to be available year-round these days, the balance of the persimmon's sweetness and tartness said to be what makes it work. A little julienned yuzu peel on top is said to bring out the aroma. Freezing it for storage is said to have made it available year-round.

## Why it took this shape
The area's mountain terrain, with its wide swing between warm days and cold nights, is said to suit drying persimmons, and rows of them hanging under the eaves have become a mark of autumn there. In the district known for the dried fruit, using it in this New Year's namasu dish is said to be an essential custom, a scene said to have continued for some 300 years. The drying racks are a common sight at the foot of two mountain ranges in the area. Their appearance under the eaves is said to mark the arrival of autumn.

sources.title: 干し柿なます 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
ツガニと呼ばれるモクズガニを米と一緒に炊き込んだごはん。ご飯に染み込んだカニの風味が持ち味とされ、別名でも呼ばれているという。産卵のため川を下る秋から冬にかけて味がよくなるとされる。はさみに藻屑のような毛が密集しているのが特徴だという。「がね飯」「かに飯」とも呼ばれているという。産卵のため川を下る時期に特に美味しくなるとされる。

## どう作るのか
一晩水につけて汚物を吐かせたツガニをたわしで洗い、甲羅を剥がしエラを除いて二つ割りにする。釜に米と水、塩や醤油を加え、下処理したカニを並べて炊き上げる。カニが赤くならない程度で火を止めるとうまみが逃げないという。カニが苦手な人は生きたまま鍋に入れて火にかける方法もあるそうだ。塩ゆでや煮付けにして食べることもあるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
昔は鶏をさばくよりもツガニを調理する方が簡単だったため、お祝いで人が集まる時に重宝されていたと伝わる。近年はとれる量が少なくなっており、資源を増やすための放流も続けられているという。玉島川など特定の川でよくとれることでも知られているそうだ。竹でつくった筌と呼ばれる道具で獲っていたと伝わる。資源を増やすための放流も毎年続けられているそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Rice is cooked together with tsugani, a mitten crab, giving the dish its character from the crab's flavor soaking into the rice; it's also known by other local names, and the crab is said to taste best from autumn into winter, when it migrates downriver to spawn. It's known for the dense, moss-like fuzz packed onto its claws. It's also known by a couple of other local names for crab rice. It's said to taste best when the crab migrates downriver to spawn.

## How it's made
The crabs are soaked overnight to purge them, scrubbed clean, and split in half after removing the shell and gills. Rice, water, salt or soy sauce, and the prepared crab are combined in a pot and cooked together. Stopping the heat just before the crab turns fully red is said to keep its savor from cooking away, and for those squeamish about handling the crab live, it can be added to the pot before the heat goes on. The crab is also said to be enjoyed simply salt-boiled or simmered on its own.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to have once been simpler to prepare than dressing a chicken, making it a convenient choice when guests gathered for a celebration. In recent years the catch has reportedly grown smaller, and the crabs are being released back into rivers to help the population recover. A particular river is said to be especially well known for the catch. It's said to have once been caught using a traditional bamboo trap. Crabs are also released back into rivers each year to help the population recover.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
エビに似たシャコ科の甲殻類「しゃっぱ」を醤油で煮つけたもの。あっさりとした身で、ゆでてすしにすることもポピュラーだという。エビ漁の網にかかり雑魚として扱われることもあるとされる。前足がカマキリのようなハサミの形をしているのが特徴だという。「がねしゃっぱ」と呼ばれることもあるという。泥底に巣穴を掘ってすむ甲殻類だとされる。

## どう作るのか
水洗いしたしゃっぱの水気をよく切り、醤油や酒などの調味料で煮る。うまみを含んだ煮汁はそうめんの漬け汁としても美味しいという。漁期の4月から10月にとれたものが旬とされる。泥底に掘ったU字形の巣穴にすんでいるそうだ。小魚やエビなどを前足で捕食しているとされる。水気をよく切ることが味を大きく左右するという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
クルマエビなどの網にかかり雑魚として扱われることもあったというしゃっぱだが、エビのようなうまみがあり、夏の味覚として親しまれてきたと伝わる。ゆでてすしにする食べ方は、あっさりとした味わいと酢の相性がよいためだとされる。北海道から沖縄まで日本全土に生息する甲殻類だという。雑魚として扱われながらも夏の味覚として愛されてきたそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Shappa, a mantis shrimp locally caught in the Ariake Sea, is simmered in soy sauce; its light, clean flesh is also popularly boiled and used for sushi. It's said to often turn up caught alongside prawns and be treated as an incidental catch, known for front legs shaped like a mantis's grasping claws. It's also sometimes called by a slightly different local nickname. It's said to dig a burrow into the muddy seabed.

## How it's made
The rinsed shrimp are drained well and simmered in a seasoning of soy sauce and sake. The flavorful cooking liquid is said to also work well as a dipping sauce for somen noodles. It's in season during its fishing period from April to October, and it's said to live in a U-shaped burrow it digs into the muddy seabed. It's said to use its front legs to catch small fish and shrimp. Draining it well is said to make a real difference to the flavor.

## Why it took this shape
Shappa is said to often turn up caught alongside prawns and was sometimes treated as an incidental catch, yet its shrimp-like savoriness has made it a favored taste of summer in the area. Boiling it for sushi is said to work especially well thanks to how its light flavor pairs with vinegar. The species is found in coastal waters all across Japan, from north to south. Treated as an incidental catch, it's nonetheless cherished as a taste of summer.

sources.title: しゃっぱの煮つけ 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
有明海にしかいないとされるワラスボを使った味噌汁。腹わたで身を炒めてからだし汁を加え、味噌を溶いて刻んだニラやねぎを散らす。目が退化し鋭い歯を持つ独特な見た目の魚だとされる。内臓や血管が透けて見える紫色の体をしているという。ハゼの仲間とされ、河口部の泥に巣穴を掘ってすむという。干潟の泥の中に巣穴を掘ってすむ魚だとされる。

## どう作るのか
ぶつ切りにしたワラスボを内臓を取り除いて塩でもみ洗いする。腹わたでワラスボを炒め、だし汁を加えて煮る。味噌を溶き、ニラやねぎを散らす。玉ねぎやじゃがいもを加えることもあるという。だしを使わずワラスボのうまみだけでつくることもあるそうだ。生きた状態から調理することが多いとされる。だしを使わずに仕上げる家庭もあるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
干満差のある干潟で川の栄養をたっぷり蓄えて育つため味がよいとされる。伝統漁法「スボカキ」で獲る姿は夏の風物詩と伝わる。凶暴な性質から取り扱いの難しい食材のひとつだったという。乾燥させてふりかけにするなど、別の食べ方も伝わっているそうだ。あんこう網にかかることも多いと伝わる。伝統漁法で漁をする姿は夏の風物詩とされる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Warasubo, a fish said to be found only in the Ariake Sea, goes into this miso soup, first stir-fried in its own innards before dashi is added, then finished with dissolved miso and scattered chives or scallion. It's known for a striking look, with degenerated eyes and sharp bared teeth, its purplish body translucent enough to show its innards and blood vessels. It's a relative of the goby and is said to burrow into the mud near river mouths.

## How it's made
The fish is cut into chunks, gutted, and rubbed clean with salt. It's stir-fried in its own innards, then simmered with dashi added. Miso is dissolved in, and chives or scallion are scattered on top; onion or potato are sometimes added too, and some versions skip the dashi entirely, relying on the fish's own savor alone. It's often cooked starting from a live fish, which takes some nerve. Some households are said to skip the dashi and rely on the fish's own flavor alone.

## Why it took this shape
The fish is said to taste good because it grows on nutrient-rich tidal flats shaped by a wide swing between high and low tide. Catching it with a traditional rake-like tool is described as a mark of summer along the coast, and its fierce temperament is said to have made it a notoriously tricky fish to handle. It's also said to be dried and turned into a seasoning to sprinkle over rice. It's also said to often turn up caught in nets set for monkfish. Catching it with the traditional method is described as a mark of summer.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
10キロほどの魚体をもつアラを丸ごと煮た姿煮。全国的にはクエと呼ばれ、透明感のある白身は姿煮のほか刺身や鍋にも向くとされる。一年中手に入るが、10月から12月が旬とされる。唐津くんちのもてなし料理として知られているそうだ。全国的には「クエ」の名で知られる高級魚だという。唐津の秋祭りに欠かせない一品として知られているという。

## どう作るのか
アラの肝を取り出し、空いた腹に大根を詰める。アラが丸ごと入る大鍋で、醤油や酒、砂糖を合わせた煮汁をかけながら一日かけて少しずつ煮込み、みりんで味を調える。大きな魚を扱うため下ごしらえには手間がかかるという。煮汁をかけ続けるのがこつとされる。煮汁を1日かけてかけ続けるのが本来のつくり方とされる。大きな魚を扱うため下ごしらえに手間がかかるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
秋祭りで日頃お世話になっている人をもてなす料理のひとつと伝わる。大きく見栄えのするアラを煮付ける習わしが始まりとされ、祭りの時期がちょうど旬と重なることも重宝された理由だという。唐津の町の女性たちが用意する祭り料理のひとつとされている。神輿とだんじりが組み合う勇壮な秋祭りとも縁が深い料理だという。日頃の付き合いに感謝する意味も込められているそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This dish simmers a whole grouper weighing around 10kg; the translucent white flesh works equally well simmered whole, as sashimi, or in a hotpot. It's available year-round but said to be at its best from October to December, and it's known as one of the dishes served for guests at a well-known autumn festival. The fish is known nationally by a different name and prized as a high-grade catch. It's known as an essential dish for a well-known autumn festival in the city.

## How it's made
The liver is removed and daikon packed into the emptied belly. The whole fish goes into a pot large enough to hold it, ladled over a day with a simmering sauce of soy sauce, sake, and sugar, finished with a touch of mirin to round out the flavor. Handling a fish this large is said to take real effort in the prep work, and basting it steadily is said to be the trick. Basting it with the simmering sauce over the course of a full day is said to be the traditional method. Handling such a large fish is said to take real effort.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to be one of the dishes served at an autumn festival to thank people a household has relied on through the year. The custom of simmering a large, impressive fish is said to be how it began, helped along by the fact that the fish happens to be in season around festival time. It's described as one of the dishes the town's women traditionally prepared for the festival. It's a dish closely tied to a spirited autumn festival built around a procession of floats. It's also said to carry a note of gratitude toward people a household has relied on.

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
もち米でついた餅に、よもぎを合わせてつくる餅菓子。あんこを包んでいただき、「ふつ」とはよもぎを指す言葉だという。春にとっての手の届く場所で摘んだよもぎを使い、各家庭でつくられてきたと伝わる。全国有数のもち米の産地でもある土地の菓子だとされる。「よもぎ餅」と呼ばれる菓子とほぼ同じものだという。全国有数のもち米の産地として知られる土地の菓子だという。

## どう作るのか
もち米を蒸して餅をついておく。ゆでてすったよもぎと合わせてさらによくつき、1つ分を手にとって伸ばし、あんこを包む。よもぎは塩少々と重曹を入れた湯でゆで、冷水にさらしてからすり鉢でペースト状にしておくという。よもぎの緑が鮮やかに仕上がるとされる。とっ手のないかごを持ってよもぎを摘みに行ったと伝わる。よもぎの緑が鮮やかに仕上がるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
稲作の盛んな土地でもち米も広く栽培され、もち米を使った郷土食のひとつとして伝わってきたという。春に摘んだよもぎを使い、桃の節句などのお供えとしてもつくられてきたそうだ。全国的には菱餅を供える地域が多い中、この土地ならではの供え物だとされる。端午の節句や花祭りの供え物としてもつくられてきたそうだ。桃の節句の供え物として親しまれてきたそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Pounded glutinous rice mochi is mixed with mugwort into a confection wrapped around sweet bean paste; futsu is a local word for mugwort, said to have been gathered by hand each spring from around the rice paddies for making at home. It's said to be a confection distinctive to a region counted among the country's leading producers of glutinous rice. It's essentially the same confection widely known elsewhere as mugwort mochi. It comes from a region counted among the country's leading producers of glutinous rice.

## How it's made
Glutinous rice is steamed and pounded into mochi. Boiled, ground mugwort is worked in and pounded further, then portioned by hand, stretched, and wrapped around sweet bean paste. The mugwort is boiled in water with a pinch of salt and baking soda, then rinsed in cold water and ground into a paste, said to give the mochi its vivid green color. Mugwort was traditionally gathered by hand into a handleless basket carried into the fields. The mugwort is said to give the mochi its vivid green color.

## Why it took this shape
In a region known for rice farming, glutinous rice is also grown widely, and this is said to be one of the local dishes built around it. Made with mugwort picked in spring, it's also said to have been offered for the Doll's Festival and similar occasions, a local alternative where diamond-shaped mochi is more common elsewhere in Japan. It's also said to have been made as an offering for the Boys' Festival and a Buddhist spring celebration, as well as the Doll's Festival.

sources.title: ふつもち 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
高菜を塩漬けにした保存食を塩抜きし、油で炒めた一品。別の呼び名でも呼ばれ、家庭で簡単につくれる定番のご飯のおともという。古漬けを塩出ししてから使うため、減塩にもつながるとされる。春は高菜漬、夏はうり漬けなど、季節ごとに違う漬物をつくる土地柄だという。「おくもじ」と呼ぶ地域もあるという。季節ごとに違う漬物を仕込む土地柄が背景にあるという。

## どう作るのか
塩漬けの高菜は水に一晩漬けて塩出しし、よく絞って刻む。ごま油で炒め、砂糖や醤油で味をつけ、ちりめんじゃこやごまを加える。高菜の塩加減に合わせて調味料の量を調整するという。お好みで唐辛子を入れることもあるそうだ。3月から4月にかけて漬け込む高菜が使われるという。ピリ辛にアレンジする家庭もあるとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
季節ごとに漬物を仕込み一年中途切れないようにする土地柄で、古くなった菜漬をおいしく食べる工夫から生まれたと伝わる。ご飯に混ぜておにぎりにしたり、ピラフやチャーハンにすることもあるという。県内の飲食店では定食の香の物として添えられることも多いそうだ。冬には大根漬けをつくる習わしもあるそうだ。ご飯に混ぜておにぎりにすることもあるそうだ。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This dish takes salt-preserved mustard greens, soaks out the salt, and stir-fries them in oil; also called by another local name, it's an easy staple to make at home as a side for rice. Soaking out the salt from the old pickles first is said to also mean less sodium in the finished dish. The region is known for pickling a different vegetable each season, from mustard greens to melon. In some areas the dish and its main ingredient are called by a slightly different name. The dish grew out of a region where a different pickle is prepared each season.

## How it's made
The salted mustard greens are soaked in water overnight to remove the salt, squeezed dry, and chopped. They're stir-fried in sesame oil, seasoned with sugar and soy sauce, and finished with small dried fish or sesame seeds; the seasoning is adjusted to how salty the greens still are, sometimes with a bit of chili for heat. The greens used are typically salted in early spring. Some households are said to spice it up with chili for a bolder version.

## Why it took this shape
In a region where pickles are prepared season by season so there's always something on hand, this dish is said to have come from finding a good way to use up greens that had aged in their brine. It's also mixed into rice balls or turned into a pilaf or fried rice, and local restaurants are said to often serve it as a pickled side with a set meal. Winter is also said to bring its own custom of pickling daikon in the same rotation. It's also mixed into rice and shaped into rice balls.

sources.title: おこもじの油炒め 佐賀県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
小麦のうまみと香りが強く、シャキシャキとしたコシが特徴とされるそうめんを冷やして食べる料理。氷水でしっかり締めることでその特徴が際立つという。ゆでても煮くずれしないため冬はにゅうめんとしても楽しまれるそうだ。九州を代表するそうめんの産地として知られているという。380年ほど前に製法が伝わったとされる歴史を持つという。

## どう作るのか
たっぷりの沸騰した湯でゆで、ざるにあげたら氷水でしっかりと締めてぬめりをとる。めんつゆにつけ、しょうがやみょうがなどの薬味とともにいただく。温暖な気候と上質な水源が小麦栽培に適していたとされる。豊富な水量を生かした水車で小麦をひいていたとも伝わる。薬味にはしょうがやみょうががよく合うとされる。小豆島の僧が製法を伝えたのが始まりとされる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
諸国を行脚していた僧が地元の行商人に手延べそうめんの製法を伝えたのが始まりと伝わる。初期は冬の農家の副業として手づくりされ、その後水車を使って小麦をひくようになったという。ロール式の製麺機をいち早く導入した、機械そうめん発祥の地とも語られている。かつては300軒を超える製麺所があったと伝わる。水車を使って小麦をひく技術も広まったという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
This chilled somen is known for a strong wheat flavor and aroma with a firm, springy bite, qualities said to come through best once the noodles are properly shocked in ice water. Because it holds up well even boiled, it's also enjoyed in a warm broth during winter, and the town is known as one of the leading somen-producing areas in Kyushu. The noodle-making technique is said to trace back roughly 380 years.

## How it's made
The noodles are boiled in plenty of water, drained, and then chilled firmly in ice water to remove the surface slipperiness. They're dipped in a noodle sauce and eaten with garnishes like ginger and myoga. The area's mild climate and good water source are said to have suited wheat cultivation well, and its ample water supply is said to have once powered mills that ground the wheat. Ginger and myoga are said to pair especially well as garnish. The technique is said to have been introduced by a traveling monk from a small island.

## Why it took this shape
The method is said to trace back to a traveling monk who taught the hand-stretched noodle technique to a local peddler who cared for him. It's said to have started as a winter side occupation for farming families, made by hand before water-powered mills later took over grinding the wheat. The town is also described as the birthplace of machine-made somen, an early adopter of roller noodle machines. The town is said to have once been home to more than 300 noodle workshops. The use of water-powered mills to grind the wheat is also said to have spread from there.
